periods.analysis: Harborview held a green status in 2024-Q3, which tells me the transparency rhythm is doing what Council asked it to do: report on time, keep the story clear, and make department work visible without adding noise. The Q3 ClearPoint certification cycle closed on schedule, with Finance, Public Works, Community Development, and Parks all submitting updates before the internal September 18 cutoff. Data quality remained strong after the Strategy Office completed spot-checks on 42 objective narratives and corrected only minor formatting issues, not substance. This is a steady green baseline rather than a victory lap, and it gives us a clean starting point for the next seven quarters.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the quarterly certification calendar and keep the two-week department review window in place, because it is working. Extend the Q3 data-quality checklist to every department liaison before the 2024-Q4 close so the process stays consistent as year-end workload rises. I recommend we add a short Council-facing “what changed this quarter” note to the dashboard packet to keep the public story crisp.

periods.analysis: Harborview stayed green in 2024-Q4, a quarter-over-quarter hold from 2024-Q3, and the year-end close was orderly. The annual dashboard refresh was completed alongside the budget book crosswalk, which helped Financial Stewardship measures line up cleanly with the City Strategic Plan. Department liaisons used the new narrative checklist well; the Clerk’s Office and IT caught three stale links before publication, which is exactly the kind of quiet quality control that builds trust. With the AA bond rating context in mind, timely and understandable reporting remains part of how we show residents and rating reviewers that Harborview manages growth deliberately.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the year-end dashboard and budget-book crosswalk as a standard December control. Extend link validation and source-document checks to the public transparency portal before each Council packet is finalized. For 2025-Q1, I recommend locking reporting assignments by January 10 so departments start the new year with no ambiguity.

periods.analysis: Harborview remained green in 2025-Q1, continuing the green-to-green movement from 2024-Q4 and showing that the process held through a new calendar year. We completed the January liaison reset with 23 departmental owners and alternates, including new contacts in Permitting and Fleet, so accountability did not depend on one person remembering everything. The ClearPoint structure stayed clean after the Q1 archive, with retired initiatives moved to the 2024 folder and active items left visible for Council review. I am especially pleased that departments are starting to use the scorecard as a management tool, not just a reporting requirement.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the January liaison reset and make it an annual governance step. Extend the archive protocol by adding a naming convention for attachments, especially for permits, procurement memos, and capital project updates. Before 2025-Q2, I recommend a 30-minute refresher for all liaison alternates so vacation season does not create reporting gaps.

periods.analysis: Harborview held green again in 2025-Q2, marking four consecutive green quarters from 2024-Q3 through 2025-Q2. The Q2 cycle absorbed heavy spring activity—budget hearings, marina-season staffing, and the permit surge along Bayshore Corridor—without slipping the reporting calendar. Data quality improved in a very practical way: Community Development began attaching Accela export dates to its dashboard notes, and Public Works added asset IDs for capital updates where relevant. That level of specificity makes departments look good because the evidence is right there, easy to verify, and ready for Council questions.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the department evidence-note practice and make export dates required on any dashboard item fed by a source system. Extend the Public Works asset-ID habit to Facilities and Parks capital items, starting with City Hall HVAC phases and Seaview Park lighting. I recommend scheduling Q3 narrative drafting one week earlier than usual to stay ahead of summer absences.

periods.analysis: Harborview remained green in 2025-Q3, continuing the stable green trend from 2025-Q2. The earlier summer drafting window worked: all departments met the August 29 internal deadline despite vacations, special events, and waterfront construction traffic. The Strategy Office ran a mid-cycle ClearPoint cleanup and removed duplicate initiative tags from 17 records, which made the Council dashboard easier to navigate. This quarter also showed stronger ownership from departments, with Police, Library, and Utilities each bringing proposed wording before I had to send the friendly reminder.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the early Q3 drafting window every year, because it protected the publication date without creating drama. Extend the duplicate-tag cleanup into a semiannual scorecard hygiene task, with IT providing a short exception report each March and September. For 2025-Q4, I recommend asking each department to identify one public-facing accomplishment and one constraint so the year-end narrative stays balanced.

periods.analysis: Harborview stayed green in 2025-Q4, a quarter-over-quarter hold from 2025-Q3 and a strong close to the 2025 reporting year. The year-end Council packet included accomplishments and constraints as planned, and that made the story more credible than a list of wins alone. Finance and the Strategy Office reconciled strategic-plan language with the preliminary audit calendar, helping preserve a clean line between performance reporting and financial stewardship. The process is now mature enough that most follow-up questions are about policy direction, not missing data, which is where we want Council attention to be.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the balanced accomplishment-and-constraint format for year-end reporting. Extend the Finance reconciliation step to include grant-funded initiatives, especially where ARPA closeout files or state transportation reimbursements support the narrative. I recommend creating a 2026 reporting calendar by December 20 and pre-loading all due dates in ClearPoint so the next cycle begins visibly and calmly.

periods.analysis: Harborview remained green in 2026-Q1, continuing the green status from 2025-Q4 and showing that the pre-loaded calendar did its job. ClearPoint reminders went out automatically to 31 owners and contributors, and only two updates needed same-day nudges from the Strategy Office. The new grant-funded initiative review helped departments separate confirmed results from pending reimbursements, which is a small but important discipline for accountable government. As Harborview keeps growing, this kind of boring-on-purpose reporting infrastructure is one of the ways we keep the public record dependable.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the pre-loaded ClearPoint deadline calendar and keep automated reminders at 14 days, 7 days, and 48 hours before close. Extend the grant review checklist to capital projects supported by bond proceeds so language remains precise for residents, auditors, and rating observers. I recommend piloting a one-page public dashboard summary for the 2026-Q2 Council agenda packet.

periods.analysis: Harborview closed 2026-Q2 green, maintaining the green-to-green movement from 2026-Q1 and completing eight straight green quarters in this sequence. The pilot one-page public dashboard summary was included with the June Council packet and gave readers a plain-language entry point before they opened the full scorecard. Departments supported it well: Finance verified AA bond rating language, Communications checked accessibility formatting, and Public Works supplied project context without overloading the page. The main takeaway is steady but meaningful progress—our reporting system is timely, sourced, readable, and increasingly useful for decision-making.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the one-page public dashboard summary for each regular quarterly update and post it with the full scorecard on the transparency portal. Extend accessibility review to all embedded charts and PDFs before 2026-Q3 publication, with Communications owning the final check. I recommend adding a short department liaison debrief after Q3 close so we capture what is working before the next year-end cycle begins.

periods.analysis: The open data portal is progressing at 65%, but the performance management policy update is at 50% and director comments remain outstanding. A September dashboard must disclose those gaps as well as completed work.
periods.recommendations: Obtain the missing director comments and retain source and status checks before issuing the Council briefing book.
